subject: Model derivative/data use — proposed carve-out and e-sign next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@projectnova.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: legal-ops@projectnova.com
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline — prohibition on model training/use for derivatives

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the overview on Friday. Our legal team sent over a short redline of your standard DPA (attached) — the core ask is simple: Project Nova cannot permit any use of our Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models or model families that would affect outputs for other customers. In particular we want an explicit carve-out that says: "Customer Data and any Derived Data shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or update any machine learning model (including foundation models) that is then used to serve other customers or published externally."

We also asked for:
- a clear definition of "Derived Data" and whether that includes embeddings and cached prompts;
- an assurance about international transfer (we prefer EU controller-to-processor agreements); and
- a list of subprocessors and standard 30-day notice for additions.

Attached is our annotated DPA for your review. Please confirm whether you can accept the no-training carve-out (or propose alternative narrow language) and whether Redwood is comfortable executing via DocuSign. We need to close this before the procurement committee call next week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Legal Ops, Project Nova
[jordan.lee@projectnova.com]

[Attachment: ProjectNova_DPA_redline_20260412.pdf (PDF, 183KB)]

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@projectnova.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — prohibition on model training/use for derivatives

Jordan — thanks, got your redline and the asks. Looping Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (legal liaison) to align on language and timing.

Short summary of where we stand: Redwood’s standard DPA already prohibits customer-identifiable data from being used to train models unless customers opt in; however, our standard language does allow aggregated telemetry and system-level improvements that don’t contain customer data. I want to be explicit and fast: if Project Nova requires an enforceable, express "no-train" covenant on "Customer Data" and "Derived Data" we can accept a carve-out with narrow definitions, but we need to be careful about the definition of "Derived Data" so we don’t inadvertently rule out benign observability (e.g., aggregate latency metrics).

Action items I propose:
1) Redwood proposes the following clause to replace the section you redlined: "Customer Data and any Derived Data (as defined below) shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve models or model families that are used to serve third parties or made available externally. "
2) Define "Derived Data" narrowly: "Derived Data means data that is a transformed representation of Customer Data where such transformation does not detach identifiers necessary to attribute the data to the Customer (examples: embeddings created from Customer Content are "Derived Data" under this definition)." We can iterate wording if that’s not acceptable.
3) We’ll provide a redlined DPA back to you today and (if agreed) route the final DPA via DocuSign.

I attached our counter-redline and a short memo framing the telemetry carve-out we need to keep for reliability/ops. Karthik — can you confirm the subprocessors notice period (we typically do 30 days with opt-out for regulated accounts) and whether an EU SCCs flow is needed for Project Nova?

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_response_20260412.pdf (PDF, 242KB)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — negotiation approach

Quick internal note (keeping it crisp):
- Sales position: accept an explicit, signed "no-training-for-others" carve-out limited to "Customer Content" + "Customer Identifiers" and allow standard "Operational Telemetry" (aggregated, non-identifiable). That keeps Project Nova happy and preserves our ability to run diagnostics and maintain platform health.
- Legal ask: tighten the definition of "Derived Data" so it explicitly calls out embeddings and cached prompts as "Derived Data" (so they’re covered by the prohibition if PN insists). If PN won’t allow the narrow definition we proposed, we should try for a contractual exception where Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated metrics only for system improvements.
- Subprocessor notice: we do 30 days for public marketplace/hosted; for enterprise we can agree to 30 days plus immediate notice for changes affecting EU data flows. Karthik — can you confirm the SCCs/EU transfer mechanism (standard practice is SCCs + DPA appendix).

If you want, I’ll send the clean proposed clause to Jordan and offer a DocuSign execution if they accept. I recommend we send the redline first, not the DocuSign, to make sure legal signs off on the exact language.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: Redwood_no-train_proposal.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — prohibition on model training/use for derivatives

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Per the attachments below, we reviewed your redline and have produced a narrow, mutually enforceable clause that Redwood is comfortable signing that:

- Explicitly prohibits using Customer Data or Defined Derived Data to train, fine-tune, or update models that are used to serve third parties;
- Defines "Derived Data" to include embeddings and any representation that would allow re-identification or reproduction of Customer Content; and
- Preserves the right for Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry strictly for platform reliability and non-model training diagnostics.

Please find attached: our redlined DPA (PDF) and a short summary memo. If this looks good, I’ve initiated the DocuSign envelope for the finalized DPA: https://app.docusign.com/1234abcd-ProjectNova-DPA (signature requested: Jordan Lee, Project Nova). HubSpot deal: https://crm.redwood.ai/hubspot/PN-4827 — please confirm once signed so we can move to onboarding.
